disputed: The DHS video's 'hunt them down' language was explicitly directed at 'EVERY CRIMINAL ILLEGAL ALIEN IN AMERICA,' not at U.S. citizens by its own text — the citizen-harm connection comes from separate, well-documented enforcement outcomes (wrongful citizen detentions, the Minneapolis shootings) rather than DHS's stated target. Whether the pattern of citizen detentions/shootings reflects deliberate policy versus poor training/recruitment (officer training cut from 16 weeks to ~6.5 weeks amid a hiring surge, per Senate letter) is a matter of dispute between DHS's public statements (emphasizing criminal removals and citing success statistics) and Congressional Democrats' and news investigations' framing (systemic recklessness). DHS disputed at least one high-profile 'wrong home' citizen-targeting claim (Oklahoma raid) as inaccurate reporting.

items: On July 28, 2025, DHS posted a video to its official X account showing Border Patrol's special operations group in tactical gear, captioned as a warning to 'EVERY CRIMINAL ILLEGAL ALIEN IN AMERICA' that they were coming to 'hunt them down.' The video overlaid a Bible verse (Proverbs 28:1: 'The wicked flee when no man pursueth; but the righteous are bold as a lion') with the opening monologue from the film 'The Batman' ('They think I'm hiding in the shadow, but I am the shadow'). Secretary Kristi Noem, a self-described conservative Christian, has publicly tied her faith to her DHS leadership. (Religion News Service)
sections.label: DHS "hunt them down" video (July 2025)

items: Despite ICE policy stating it 'cannot assert its civil immigration enforcement authority to arrest and/or detain a U.S. citizen,' multiple citizens have been wrongly stopped, detained, or deported since enforcement escalated in 2025; 48 House Democrats, led by Sens. Warren, Padilla and Kelly and Reps. Correa and Goldman, formally asked DHS's Inspector General in August 2025 to investigate the pattern, citing CNN and Washington Post reporting on citizens being detained. (Sen. Warren press release; letter to DHS OIG)

In January 2026, ICE agents fatally shot two U.S. citizens, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, in Minneapolis; a New York Times report found the man killed was holding a phone, not a gun. A Senate letter to Secretary Noem (Sens. Heinrich, Welch and others) stated ICE agents had shot 12 people since September 2025 (4 fatal), that 2025 was ICE's deadliest custody year in two decades (32 deaths, per a Guardian analysis), with CBP reporting 17 more deaths, and tied this to officer training being cut from 16 weeks to about 6.5 weeks amid a hiring surge of over 12,000 new ICE officers since January 2025. The letter also cited a May 2025 ICE memo (only publicly reported later) directing agents to enter residences without judicial warrants. (Sen. Heinrich letter to Noem; Sen. Welch press release; NYT; NBC News; The Guardian)
sections.label: Enforcement harms to U.S. citizens

summary: DHS has used explicitly militarized 'hunt them down' language — paired with religious and pop-culture references — in official messaging about immigration enforcement, while separately, ICE/CBP enforcement under reduced training standards has resulted in U.S. citizens being wrongly detained, and in at least two cases (Minneapolis, Jan. 2026) fatally shot, drawing formal congressional oversight demands.
title: DHS "hunt them down" messaging and enforcement harms to U.S. citizens
